chunks: I said to Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: A man has one hundred and ninety-nine dirhams and nineteen dinars; does he pay zakat on them? He said: “No. There is no zakat upon him in the dirhams nor in the dinars until they become complete.”
Zurārah said: And likewise, this applies in all things.

He said: And I said to Abū ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام: A man had four she-camels, thirty-nine sheep, and twenty-nine cows; does he pay zakat on them? He said: “He does not pay anything of zakat on them, because none of them is complete, so zakat is not obligatory on it.”

key_terms.أَيْنُقٍ: she-camels, one category of livestock subject to zakat thresholds
key_terms.الدَّرَاهِمِ: silver dirhams, used here as zakatable monetary wealth
key_terms.الدَّنَانِيرِ: gold dinars, used here as zakatable monetary wealth
key_terms.بَقَرَةً: cow, mentioned as livestock below the zakat threshold
key_terms.تَتِمَّ: to become complete, meaning to reach the full required amount
key_terms.زَكَاةٌ: the obligatory alms-tax due only when the required threshold is met
key_terms.زُرَارَةُ: Zurārah, the narrator reporting the question and ruling
key_terms.شَاةً: sheep, mentioned as livestock below the zakat threshold

ai.seo_question: Is zakat due on wealth or livestock that is below the minimum nisab amount?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal ruling that zakat is not obligatory on wealth or livestock that has not reached its complete nisab threshold. It applies both to coined wealth such as dirhams and dinars and to animals such as camels, sheep, and cows. The narration establishes a general principle in zakat law: incompleteness of the required amount prevents obligation.
